html:
A Persian poet from Tus, in Khorasan in northeastern Iran, who wrote the Shahnameh, the "Book of Kings". It is the national epic of Iran and one of the longest poems ever written by one person.

Ferdowsi came from the dehqans, the old landowning class that kept memories of pre-Islamic Iran alive. He began the poem under the Samanids, who backed Persian culture, and worked on it for some thirty years, finishing around 1010. In about 50,000 couplets it tells the history of Iran from the first king to the fall of the Sasanian Empire in the Arab conquests, with heroes such as Rostam and his tragic fight with his son Sohrab.

He wrote in Persian with few Arabic words, at a time when Arabic ruled learned writing. The poem helped keep the Persian language and Iranian identity alive. He dedicated it to Mahmud of Ghazni, and legend says the sultan paid him poorly; when a better reward finally came, Ferdowsi's coffin was leaving the city. His tomb at Tus is a national shrine.
